messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: experimenting experimental clang 3.2 on windows
parts:
First, clang needs a gcc for the c++ library and header files included in gcc.  In particular, clang needs a special gcc that support DW2 error handling.  I do not know much about this until I hit errors when the typical gcc such as the one included in rtools does not work.  See here for a reference:
http://lists.cs.uiuc.edu/pipermail/cfe-dev/2012-August/023578.html
http://gcc.gnu.org/wiki/WindowsGCCImprovements

The gcc I am using that supports DW2 error handling is downloaded from 
http://sourceforge.net/projects/mingw-w64/files/Toolchains%20targetting%20Win32/Personal%20Builds/rubenvb/gcc-dw2-4.6-release/i686-w64-mingw32-gcc-dw2-4.6.3-1-release-win32_rubenvb.7z/download

The above gcc is build for 32 bits.  The reason might be that gcc only support DW2 error handling on 32 bits windows now (or results of some other reasons).  This might be the reason that there is only 32bits experimental clang from llvm.org.  

For the above gcc, unzip it and put it somewhere say c:\mingw32-dw2 and then add c:\mingw32-dw2\bin to the PATH environment variable. 

Second, download llvm/clang from http://llvm.org/releases/3.2/clang+llvm-3.2-x86-mingw32-EXPERIMENTAL.tar.gz, and then unzip llvm's files to the above mingw's (ie, merge two bin's, two include's, etc.)  Merging the gcc and llvm/clang seems to be the easiest way I found to avoid clang's inability to find header files of gcc's c++ library. 

It is done.  Here is an example to prove I can really use it with code that throw errors. 


C:\Users\root\Desktop>path
PATH=c:\mingw32-dw2\bin;c:\rtools\bin;C:\Rtools\gcc-4.6.3\bin;C:\Program Files\R
\R-2.15.1\bin;C:\Windows\system32;C:\Windows;C:\Windows\System32\Wbem;C:\Windows
\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\;C:\Program Files (x86)\Git\cmd;C:\Program File
s (x86)\Git\bin;C:\Program Files\MiKTeX 2.9\miktex\bin\x64\;C:\Program Files\Thi
nkPad\Bluetooth Software\;C:\Program Files\ThinkPad\Bluetooth Software\syswow64;
C:\Program Files\SlikSvn\bin;C:\Program Files (x86)\pdftk-1.44-win-install\bin;C
:\Program Files\Vim\vim73

C:\Users\root\Desktop>type a.cpp
#include <iostream>

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
  std::cout << "test." << std::endl;
  try {
    throw std::exception();
  } catch (const std::exception& e) {
  }
  return 0;
}

C:\Users\root\Desktop>clang++ a.cpp

C:\Users\root\Desktop>a.out
test.


Last, currently I cannot use this clang 3.2 to pass stan's unit tests (this might be what Ben hits on linux using clang 3.2).  And it's a pain to use this clang for R on Windows 7 64bits since 1) it does not support target of 64 bits, which the gcc in rtools supports,  2) different error handling means the need of installing Rcpp from source just for 32 bits, which needs some hack. 

--
Jiqiang

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] experimenting experimental clang 3.2 on windows
parts:
In RStan, some models can be compiled and run using this clang if Rcpp is rebuilt.  (In order to install Rcpp from source using this clang, a gcc for 64 bits such as the one in rtools is still needed since both 32 and 64 bits of Rcpp would be built by R's package installation script.) 

The problem with clang I have so far is that it fails for model src/basic_distributions/inv_wishart.  Using Stan from command line, I found the error message is "The instruction at 0x76ff99777 referenced memory at 0xffffffff. The memory could not be read."  R would crash for this model. 

Using another gcc, RStan could run all example models in Stan.  

--
